segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Morning team, this is the weekly engineering sync. Let's go through the search latency work first.

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: The new caching layer cut search latency from four hundred milliseconds to ninety milliseconds at the median.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: That's great progress. Are we seeing any cache invalidation issues?

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: One issue in staging where stale results showed for about a minute. I will add an invalidation hook on product updates by Thursday.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: On the infrastructure side, the Postgres upgrade to version sixteen is scheduled. I'm worried about the replication lag we saw last time.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Good point. We decided to run the upgrade on the read replica first and promote it after a day of monitoring.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Sounds good. I will write the runbook for the replica upgrade by tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Should we also bump the connection pool size?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: I don't know yet, let's revisit that after we see the metrics from the replica.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Mia, can you share the load test results with the team by Friday?

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: The flaky checkout test is still failing about five percent of the time, which is frustrating.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: We agreed to quarantine flaky tests and track them on the board. Leo, please create a ticket for the checkout test today.
